meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the C-201 unit
meta.scope: From the battery limit at the V-201 inlet, through P-201A/B, FV-201, E-201, C-201 with E-203, E-202, V-202 and P-202A/B, to the propane rundown (LV-203), the bottoms to the debutanizer (LV-202), the vent to fuel gas (PV-210) and the relief to flare (PSV-201); the SIS (XV-201, XV-202, XV-209) and the utilities as they enter the unit.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N5.causes:
CW pump or cooling-tower failure (site-wide)
HV-216 closed
N5.cons: Nothing condenses: pressure climbs, PSV-201 lifts at 00:27 and the model peaks at 1.868 MPa g relieving up to about 19,900 Nm³/h (6,500 Nm³ in 30 min) with no trip; V-202 drains (LIC-203 LO at 04:20, down to 0.3 %) and the reflux pumps run dry

N5.causes:
HV-210 closed by mistake
PV-210 fails closed or PIC-210 in MAN at low output
fuel-gas header blocked
N5.cons: Non-condensables accumulate and blanket E-202: pressure rises slowly (model, PV-210 closed: PIC-210 HI at 06:19, PI-211 HI at 07:37, PSV-201 lifts at 07:41, about 330 Nm³/h)

Higher condensing temperature: PV-210 vents more (and more propane with it), then the pressure rises to relief (model: CW 15 °C warmer lifts PSV-201 at 01:43, up to 6,100 Nm³/h; condenser UA −50 % lifts it at 01:52, vent up to 521 Nm³/h)

N5.causes: Methane or hydrogen from the upstream unit
N5.cons: Condenser area blanketed; PV-210 vents more gas and propane (model, five-fold: vent up to 361 Nm³/h, PIC-210 HI at 03:29, PSV-201 briefly lifts at 04:17)

N5.dev: Too much vent to fuel gas (column depressured)
N5.causes: PV-210 fails open (instrument air) or PIC-210 forced high
N5.cons: Propane vapour lost to fuel gas (model, PV-210 wide open: vent up to 483 Nm³/h, pressure down to 1.54 MPa g, PIC-210 LO at 05:20); fuel-gas header overpressure; column upset

N5.causes: Drift, impulse-line leak or blockage, calibration error
N5.cons: PV-210 acts on a wrong pressure: the true column pressure can move away from 1.70 MPa g in either direction without the control alarm seeing it

N5.causes:
Inlet or outlet isolation closed
set too high
seat damage after lifting
N5.cons: No protection against the overpressure rows above (vessel rupture), or continuous loss of propane to flare

N5.dev: External fire at C-201 or V-202
N5.causes: Pool fire from an LPG leak at the pumps or the bottoms
N5.cons: Vapour generation beyond the process cases; wall overheating above the liquid, rupture and BLEVE
LPG at 1.70 MPa g into the cooling water: flammable gas released at the cooling tower

recs.text: Relief and fire review: confirm the design pressures of V-201, V-202 and the E-201 process side (not on the P&ID); give V-201 its own PSV sized for fire, and confirm V-202 is protected by PSV-201 with no isolation between; add fireproofing, water deluge and a depressuring route for the LPG vessels (BLEVE prevention).

Gas detection around P-201A/B, P-202A/B, V-201, V-202, E-203 and the bottoms line, with remote-operated shut-off valves on the V-201 and V-202 outlets and on the column bottoms; double mechanical seals with seal-leak alarms on the LPG pumps.

High-pressure trip PSHH on two or three independent transmitters (recommended addition, 2oo3) that closes XV-209 and XV-202 (heat off) before PSV-201 lifts; LOPA to set its SIL. Today PSV-201 is the only layer against every overpressure scenario.

Flare study: loss of cooling water is common to every column on the site, so check the flare header and flare for the simultaneous relief (C-201 alone reaches about 19,900 Nm³/h in the model); back-pressure on PSV-201.
Low-low level on V-202 (LSLL-203, recommended addition) that stops P-202A/B before they run dry.
Car-seal HV-210 open (CSO register) and add a PIC-210 output-high alarm: a vent that cannot open leaves the column to PSV-201.
Fuel-gas interface: knock-out drum on the PV-210 vent before the fuel-gas header, high-flow alarm on FI-217, and tell the fuel-gas system owner that PV-210 fails open.
Deviation alarm between PIC-210 and PI-211: two independent transmitters must agree; operating note on which to believe.
PSV-201 inlet and outlet isolation valves car-sealed open; test and inspection interval; flare line free-draining.
Hydrocarbon detection on the E-202 cooling-water return: LPG leaking into the cooling water is released at the cooling tower.
Instrument-air failure: review the fail positions (PV-210 fails open to fuel gas, LV-202 and LV-203 fail closed) and consider an ESD on low air-header pressure; confirm the air receiver hold-up time.
LOPA for the High rows that rely on PSV-201, LSHH-203, LSLL-202 and on the operator (overpressure from cooling-water loss, a blocked vent or too much reflux; V-201 overfill and fire; LPG leaks).
